slot.brief: Sum an arithmetico-geometric series to n terms (or infinity) such as Σ n xⁿ; use the shift-and-subtract method; moderately demanding algebra.

verdicts.working: Using the finite geometric-sum derivative, \(\sum_{k=1}^{6}kx^{k-1}=\frac{1-7x^6+6x^7}{(1-x)^2}\). At \(x=-\tfrac12\), this equals \(\tfrac38\).

working:
Let $S=\sum_{k=1}^{6}kr^{k-1}$, where $r=-\dfrac12$. Then $(1-r)S=1+r+r^2+r^3+r^4+r^5-6r^6=\dfrac{9}{16}$. Hence $S=\dfrac{9}{16}\div\dfrac32=\dfrac38$.

Independent check: Using the finite geometric-sum derivative, \(\sum_{k=1}^{6}kx^{k-1}=\frac{1-7x^6+6x^7}{(1-x)^2}\). At \(x=-\tfrac12\), this equals \(\tfrac38\).
